title: Laser method repairs aircraft landing gear without replacing part
content: Researchers have developed a laser-based method to repair the landing gear of an aircraft, the highly stressed parts of a plane.​During takeoff, landing, and taxiing, components such as wheel axles, shock-absorbing pistons, and connecting pins endure massive forces. At the same time, bearings, bushings, and seals are subjected to constant friction and wear.​Moreover, repeated exposure to cold, heat, moisture, kerosene, cleaning and deicing agents, as well as ice, sand and dust make these aircraft surfaces more vulnerable to corrosion.​Minor damage is scraped off from the material during the routine maintenance; however, this approach can be used only up to a certain limit. Beyond that, this replacing a part is the only option, which is not only expensive but keeps the aircraft out of service for longer periods.High-speed lasers for aerospace repair​Traditionally, chromium plating has been used to protect surfaces; however, environmental and occupational safety concerns have pushed scientists to look for alternatives.​Welding parts is not a viable alternative, as excessive heat could alter the microstructure of aerospace steels and change the component geometry. ​To counter these challenges, scientists at the Fraunhofer Institute for Laser Technology ILT in Germany have devised a high-speed variant of laser metal deposition (LMD).​Extreme High-Speed Laser Material Deposition (EHLA) is a faster version of LMD that uses a laser to melt metal powder and apply it precisely where needed. The process works much faster than conventional methods while generating less heat. This makes it suitable for repairing or coating heat-sensitive, high-strength aerospace components.​The researchers turned to this modified approach that world work in real-world scenarios and beyond the laboratories.​”What matters is whether the process is suitable for real landing gear components under load, including their materials, damage patterns and repair limits,” said Harald Betsch of Liebherr-Aerospace, Senior Expert Thermal Spraying/Welding in Materials and Processes.Hard-press rollers for finish​Shortly after the laser-assisted metal deposition, the team presses a hard roller against the material rather than cutting or grinding it, a process done in a single step. The researchers called it Simultaneous Coating and Roller Burnishing (SCaRB).​”The key for us is to use the layer while it is still warm, rather than finishing the EHLA coating in a separate operation afterward,” explained Kim Julia Kallies, project manager at Fraunhofer ILT.​By smoothing and strengthening the freshly deposited, still-warm metal layer, it eliminates separate finishing steps, reduces setup time, and allows researchers to tailor surface finish, hardness, and residual stresses for repaired aircraft components.​Researchers noted that they can tune the repaired area’s hardness, surface finish, and residual stresses by adjusting process parameters, including laser power, powder feed, distance between laser and burnishing tool, burnishing force, roller radius, and hardness.​The technology is still being validated by researchers by testing the material’s durability under realistic conditions.​Beyond the repair process, the team used a laser to check coating and subsurface quality without damaging the repaired part. The method, LAwave (short for laser-induced surface acoustic wave spectroscopy), generates acoustic (sound) waves and analyzes how they travel through the material.​However, the method still requires further development to qualify for aerospace standards, as the researchers are currently testing it on real landing gear geometries under representative loads.

title: SpaceX skips Starship booster catch for Gulf of Mexico splashdown
content: SpaceX has launched its 15th Starship test flight, putting its next-generation rocket through another major test. However, the mission has already missed one of its most ambitious recovery objectives. The company did not attempt to catch the Super Heavy booster at its Texas launch tower.Instead, the massive first-stage rocket headed for a splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico. Attention now shifts to Starship’s upper stage, which is targeting a return to its original launch site. A successful landing would mark a significant step toward SpaceX’s fully reusable rocket ambitions.Booster recovery takes backseatStarship lifted off from SpaceX’s Starbase facility in South Texas on Friday. Its Super Heavy booster initially powered the vehicle using 33 Raptor engines. The engines supplied the thrust needed to push the 40-story rocket through Earth’s atmosphere.The vehicle subsequently passed through Max Q, the point of maximum aerodynamic pressure during ascent. This milestone subjects a rocket to particularly intense structural stress. Starship cleared the challenging phase before reaching another critical flight event.Super Heavy then shut down its main engines as the upper stage prepared to separate. Starship ignited its own engines during a maneuver known as hot staging. This technique uses upper-stage thrust to help separate the two sections.Following separation, Super Heavy began its return trajectory. SpaceX initially appeared positioned to attempt another mechanical-arm recovery. However, the company ultimately directed the booster toward a controlled splashdown.SpaceX’s Dan Huot confirmed that 32 booster engines remained operational during the flight. The decision to forgo the tower catch means the mission will not demonstrate another successful first-stage recovery.Upper stage faces crucial testStarship’s upper stage now carries the mission’s most significant recovery objective. SpaceX plans to bring the spacecraft back to its Texas launch facility. The return attempt should take place approximately 22 hours after liftoff.If successful, the spacecraft will descend toward its original launch tower. Its onboard engines will control the final approach. Giant mechanical arms, nicknamed chopsticks, will then attempt to capture the returning vehicle.Super Heavy has diverted to an offshore splashdown in the Gulf pic.twitter.com/1M2xn7NYJA— SpaceX (@SpaceX) November 13, 2026Recovering the upper stage would represent a major engineering achievement. SpaceX has previously demonstrated successful Super Heavy booster catches. However, bringing Starship itself back to the launch tower presents another level of complexity.The spacecraft must withstand atmospheric reentry before executing its final landing maneuver. Its previous flight in September ended with an intact Pacific Ocean splashdown. That mission lasted approximately three hours despite an initial 10-hour flight plan.Reusability remains the goalStarship’s latest mission also carries commercial significance. The spacecraft deployed another batch of operational Starlink satellites during its orbital flight. September’s mission marked the first time Starship carried operational satellites into orbit.That capability could eventually help SpaceX expand its satellite internet network. The company also envisions using Starship to deploy orbital computing infrastructure. Its proposed Starmind network would involve data-processing centers operating in space.However, reliable recovery remains essential to Starship’s long-term economics. SpaceX wants to recover both rocket stages and prepare them for subsequent flights. Achieving that goal could reduce launch costs and shorten turnaround times.Friday’s flight has delivered another orbital mission for the developing rocket. The booster recovery objective remains unfulfilled, leaving the upper-stage landing as the next major milestone. Its outcome could determine how much progress Starship has made toward complete vehicle reusability.

title: New Orleans tanker collision capsizes cruise ship with 129 passengers
content: A collision between a commercial tanker and a docked river cruise ship sent passengers into the Mississippi River on Friday, triggering a large-scale rescue operation in New Orleans. The impact overturned the cruise vessel, leaving part of it submerged as emergency crews rushed to recover people from the water.The incident involved Atlantic Asphalt’s tanker and American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage near the French Quarter. Officials said approximately 129 passengers were aboard the 295-foot vessel when the collision occurred around 12:30 p.m. local time.Tanker strikes docked vesselThe American Heritage had arrived at the port roughly two hours earlier. Passengers had begun disembarking when the tanker struck its side, according to port officials.🚨 BREAKING NEWS 🚨The NOFD responded to a tanker and riverboat incident near Port of New Orleans HQ. A three-alarm response (23 units, 57 personnel) was dispatched to rescue passengers and crew, assisting with triage and transport.📸 Retired District Chief Chris Mickal pic.twitter.com/TL4pmkgjnO— New Orleans Fire Department (@NOLAFireDept) November 13, 2026The collision caused the riverboat to capsize. First responders arriving at the scene found passengers in the water and began rescue operations. The New Orleans Fire Department led efforts alongside local EMS and police personnel. The U.S. Coast Guard also joined the emergency response.Mayor Helena Moreno’s office confirmed that rescuers had pulled multiple people from the water. Officials also reported injuries, although authorities had not released a confirmed casualty count.Investigators examine collisionAmerican Cruise Lines confirmed the collision and said crews evacuated guests and staff. The company also expressed concern for everyone involved.Investigators are now examining what caused the tanker to hit the cruise ship. An emergency response source suggested the tanker may have experienced a power failure before impact. However, officials have not confirmed that possibility.Our hearts are with the passengers, crew, and families affected by this afternoon’s collision between a passenger vessel and a tanker on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, near the Crescent City Connection.Coast Guard crews are on scene with the New Orleans Fire Department,…— U.S. Coast Guard (@USCG) November 13, 2026Authorities have yet to establish the full extent of the damage or determine how many people suffered injuries.All passengers accounted forAll passengers aboard the American Heritage have been accounted for following Friday’s collision, which sent the cruise ship capsizing into the Mississippi River in New Orleans. Officials described the rescue as a “miracle on the Mississippi.”LCMC Health is treating 32 people injured in the collision, including 30 passengers and two officers who ended up in the water. Their injuries were reported as non-critical. Authorities also confirmed that no children were involved.Although the vessel was carrying approximately 129 passengers, some reports put the total number of people aboard, including crew members, at nearly 200. Everyone has since been accounted for, and authorities have ended the search and rescue operation.Police officers and other first responders helped evacuate passengers as the vessel began to capsize. Those who could not get off the ship in time were transferred to other boats and brought to safety.New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno praised the rescue efforts involving emergency personnel and volunteers. Hotel rooms have also been secured for passengers affected by the collision.The cause of the incident remains under investigation.

title: US flights resume after FAA lifts nationwide ground stop
content: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday night after a telecommunications failure disrupted air traffic control centers across the country, grounding departing flights and affecting thousands of journeys.The FAA initially ordered all departing flights nationwide grounded, citing “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” The restriction was imposed as a precaution after communications problems affected multiple air traffic control facilities.The ground stop was lifted at 8:15 p.m. ET after the FAA restored full functionality at its air traffic control centers and Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON) facilities. However, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy warned that it would take time for normal operations to resume.Telecommunications outage halts flightsThe FAA said the communications issues began at around 3:36 p.m. ET, affecting facilities and TRACONs across the country. The agency described the problem as a temporary telecommunications outage and said it halted departures out of an abundance of caution.Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the disruption affected multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which guide aircraft at high altitudes along their routes. FAA technicians were investigating the issue.More than 3,500 aircraft were in the air when the ground stop was issued. Pilots and air traffic controllers followed established procedures to safely land aircraft, bringing the number of planes in the affected airspace to fewer than 400 by 8 p.m. ET.The FAA clarified that it had not lost all radar or telecommunications capabilities. Exceptions were also made for critical medical evacuation flights, life-saving cargo and law enforcement aircraft.Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication that the disruption posed a threat to the United States. He later said the incident did not appear to be a cyberattack and appeared to be mechanically driven.Media reports citing flight-data firm Cirium said around 11,000 flights were scheduled to depart US airports after 4 p.m. ET on Friday. The firm also reported approximately 600 diverted flights, including 104 redirected to other airports.Ageing air traffic system faces overhaulThe disruption comes as the FAA works to modernise an air traffic control system that has faced repeated equipment failures, communications problems and controller shortages.Duffy blamed ageing air traffic control infrastructure for the latest disruption, warning that the system would continue to experience failures without upgrades. He urged Congress to approve additional funding and said returning to normal operations would take time. He added that the disruption was not expected to affect Thanksgiving travel.Congress approved $12.5 billion for the overhaul last year. The FAA and White House also sought an additional $30.1 billion on Friday to support the modernisation effort, Reuters reported.Nationwide ground stops are extremely rare. The latest disruption marked only the second nationwide halt of departures since the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. In January 2023, the FAA halted domestic departures for less than two hours following an outage in its Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) system.

title: Scientists Discover How Exercise Could Help Protect the Brain From Parkinson’s
content:
Parkinson’s disease is a progressive neurological disorder that affects movement, balance, and coordination. It develops as dopamine-producing nerve cells in the brain gradually deteriorate, leading to symptoms such as tremors, muscle stiffness, and slowed movement. Credit: Shutterstock
Exercise may offer benefits for Parkinson’s disease that extend far beyond physical movement.
Exercise may benefit people with Parkinson’s disease in ways that go far beyond building strength and improving mobility. A review of 129 studies suggests that contracting muscles release chemical messengers capable of influencing brain health, potentially helping vulnerable nerve cells resist damage.
The research highlights how regular physical activity can improve movement, balance, mood, and cognitive function while reducing falls and disability. Scientists are also investigating whether the biological changes triggered by exercise could help slow aspects of the disease itself.
How Exercising Muscles Communicate With the Brain
“Muscles do much more than move our body. They can act like an endocrine organ, producing hormone-like chemical messengers called ‘exerkines,’ which are released during exercise—just like the pancreas produces insulin or the thyroid gland produces thyroid hormones,” explains Dr. Miguel Germán Borda.
When muscles contract, they release signaling molecules known as exerkines that can travel through the bloodstream and influence organs throughout the body, including the brain, heart, liver, and immune system. Among the molecules examined in the review were brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1), irisin, cathepsin B, myostatin, and growth/differentiation factor 15 (GDF15). These substances have different biological functions, and researchers are working to understand their individual contributions to brain health.
“So, the next question became, how do exerkines protect the brain?” says Dr. Salomón Páez-García. “We found that the exerkines act as a medium for the crosstalk between the muscle and the brain. Though the brain controls muscles, exercising muscles send beneficial signals back to the brain through exerkines,” he further explains.
How Exercise May Protect Vulnerable Brain Cells
Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurological disorder characterized by the loss of dopamine-producing neurons, particularly in a brain region called the substantia nigra. This degeneration contributes to movement difficulties, while the disease can also affect thinking, mood, sleep, and other functions. With populations aging worldwide, Parkinson’s represents an increasing public health challenge.
The reviewed research suggests that certain exercise-related signaling molecules may reduce inflammation and oxidative stress, support mitochondrial function, and promote neuroplasticity, the brain’s ability to adapt and form new connections. Experimental findings indicate that these effects can help dopamine-producing neurons withstand cellular stress and damage. However, further clinical research is needed to establish whether these mechanisms meaningfully slow neurodegeneration in people with Parkinson’s.
Why Muscle Strength Matters in Parkinson’s Disease
Muscle health becomes increasingly important as Parkinson’s progresses. Sarcopenia, the gradual age-related loss of muscle mass, strength, and physical function, can contribute to frailty and disability. In people with Parkinson’s, it may also be associated with more frequent falls, greater cognitive impairment, poorer outcomes, and reduced quality of life.
The review identified benefits across several types of physical activity. Aerobic exercise, including walking and jogging, supports cardiovascular fitness, while resistance training, such as weightlifting and squats, builds muscle strength. Balance exercises, including Tai Chi and standing on one leg, improve stability. Programs combining these approaches can address multiple physical challenges simultaneously. Current Parkinson’s care guidelines recommend beginning exercise early, maintaining regular activity, and adjusting exercise programs to individual abilities as the disease progresses.
What 129 Studies Reveal About Exercise and Parkinson’s
“Muscle is a biologically active tissue that has the potential to influence neural function. Building on this, we collected experimental, observational, and interventional data that evaluated the interplay between muscle status and exercise in PD,” says Dr. Salomón Páez-García, the study’s first author.
Although exercise is already an established component of Parkinson’s management, its potential neuroprotective effects remain under investigation. Researchers still need to determine which exercise types, intensities, and durations produce the greatest long-term benefits, as well as which exerkines are most responsible for the observed biological effects.
Reference: “Exercise, exerkines, and muscle–brain crosstalk in Parkinson’s disease” by Salomón Páez-García, Edgar Alvarado, Alejandro Cuevas, Laura Valverde, Eduardo Salinas, Kevin O’Hara-Veintimilla, María Cruz Rodríguez-Oroz and Miguel Germán Borda, 25 February 2026,
Neuroprotection
DOI: 10.1002/nep3.70032

title: Scientists Develop Injectable Glucose Sensor That Could Change Diabetes Care
content:
New research centers on a nonenzymatic glucose-sensing platform that uses fluorescent molecules to measure glucose concentrations. Scientists incorporated the sensing chemistry into a small hydrogel that can be injected into the tissue and is designed to sit beneath the skin. Credit: Texas A&M University
An experimental injectable sensor could give people with diabetes a more affordable way to track blood sugar, with early tests showing that a cheaper sensing ingredient performed similarly to its costlier alternative.
For millions of people with diabetes, knowing how glucose levels are changing helps guide decisions about medication, meals, and daily activities. Continuous glucose monitors provide that information in real time, but their cost keeps the devices out of reach for some patients. Making monitoring more affordable requires attention to the materials inside a sensor, as well as how reliably they work.
Researchers at
Texas A&M University
have identified a less expensive ingredient for an experimental injectable glucose sensor. Their study, published in
ACS Measurement Science AU
, found that a sensing material costing roughly one-tenth as much as an alternative used in earlier versions delivered comparable performance.
An injectable gel holds glucose-sensing chemistry
The proposed sensor houses its sensing chemistry in a small hydrogel, a water-rich material that can be injected into tissue and sit beneath the skin. The gel provides a stable home for the sensing materials while allowing glucose to pass through. In testing, it retained more than 94% of the sensing mixture over seven days, demonstrating that the chemistry could function within an injectable platform.
“Our long-term goal is to develop a reliable, affordable injectable glucose sensor that can expand access to continuous glucose monitoring, particularly for people in under-resourced communities and those without adequate insurance coverage,” said Dr. Gérard L. Coté, the study’s principal investigator and a professor of biomedical engineering in Texas A&M’s College of Engineering. “Reducing the cost of the sensing materials is one step toward making these technologies accessible to more people who need them.”
As glucose levels rise, glucose molecules occupy more binding sites on the sensor protein, displacing fluorescent sensing molecules and changing the fluorescent signal. Credit: Texas A&M University
To measure glucose, the platform uses changes in near-infrared fluorescence, a light signal beyond the visible range. Many glucose-monitoring systems rely on enzymes, which help chemical reactions occur. This approach instead detects glucose through a competition between molecules.
Glucose and a fluorescent sugar compound compete for available binding sites on a protein called concanavalin A, or ConA. As glucose concentrations rise, more glucose molecules enter that competition, changing the fluorescent signal. This process, known as competitive binding, allows the researchers to track glucose concentrations without enzymes.
A cheaper sugar matches sensing performance
The team compared several glucose-binding compounds, including two forms of a sugar called mannopentaose. Earlier versions of the technology used α-mannopentaose. The much less expensive β-mannopentaose provided comparable sensing performance and also performed well in artificial interstitial fluid, a solution designed to mimic the environment beneath the skin.
“The surprising part was how closely the lower-cost material matched the performance of the more expensive alternative,” said Dr. Sayantan Tripathy, an assistant research scientist in Texas A&M’s Optical and Bio-Sensing Laboratory and the study’s lead author. “In this case, the cheaper option wasn’t really a compromise, and that’s an important finding when you’re thinking about future glucose-monitoring technologies.”
The injectable sensor remains experimental
The cost comparison concerns one sensing component. The technology remains at the proof-of-concept stage and needs additional development and testing before it could be considered for clinical use.
“Developing an affordable glucose sensor means considering the cost of the individual materials as well as how well they work together,” Coté said. “This study shows that we can substantially reduce the cost of one sensing component while maintaining comparable performance, giving us a promising foundation for further development.”
Reducing manufacturing costs could eventually help expand access to future diabetes-monitoring technologies. That possibility makes affordability a consideration throughout development, alongside technical performance.
“When new medical technologies are expensive, access can be limited,” said Dr. Melissa Grunlan, a study co-author, professor of biomedical engineering in the College of Engineering, and professor of chemistry in the College of Arts and Sciences. “Our goal is to develop sensors that are not only effective but affordable for the people who rely on them.”
The team plans to refine the platform and evaluate additional components that may improve its performance, longevity, and practicality.
“While the work remains in the research stage, the findings suggest that future glucose-monitoring technologies may not have to rely on expensive materials to deliver effective results,” Tripathy said.
Reference: “β-Anomeric Mannopentaose-Based Nonenzymatic NIR Glucose Sensor Enabling Cost-Effective Continuous Monitoring” by Sayantan Tripathy, Diana Al Husseini, Carolina I. Martinez, Anthony Dongchau, Samyucktha Ganesapandian, Melissa A Grunlan and Gerard L Cote, 19 August 2026,
ACS Measurement Science Au
DOI: 10.1021/acsmeasuresciau.6c00076
This research was funded by the National Science Foundation (NSF) Engineering Research Center for Precise Advanced Technologies and Health Systems for Under-resourced Populations.

title: A Simple Pill Could Cure a Common Cause of High Blood Pressure
content:
Scientists have uncovered evidence that prolonged treatment may disrupt the cells responsible for a common hormonal cause of hypertension. Credit: Shutterstock
Blood pressure stayed lower for up to two years after treatment ended in a small follow-up study, suggesting some people with hormone-driven hypertension could avoid lifelong medication.
For people with a common hormonal cause of high blood pressure, a cure has required surgery to remove an entire adrenal gland. Medication can keep their blood pressure under control, often with the prospect of taking it for life.
The condition, called primary aldosteronism, accounts for an estimated 5% to 10% of cases of high blood pressure, or hypertension, which affects millions of people worldwide. Benign nodules in the adrenal glands produce too much of the hormone aldosterone, causing the kidneys to retain excess salt and driving blood pressure up.
A study led by
Queen Mary University of London
now suggests that a limited course of medication could offer a lasting cure for some people with this condition. The approach, called extended aldosterone synthase inhibition (EASI), involves taking a new class of drugs for 6 to 12 months. These drugs block aldosterone synthase, an enzyme needed to make the hormone, targeting the excess production responsible for the hypertension.
Blood pressure improvements outlasted treatment
The findings, published in the
New England Journal of Medicine
, came from follow-up measurements in 14 people treated at eight centers across the United States. They had participated in the first study of this drug class in people with primary aldosteronism, also led by Queen Mary and reported last year in the same journal. Researchers subsequently examined routine measurements of their blood pressure and hormone levels to see how they compared with values recorded before treatment.
For up to two years after treatment ended, hormone levels and blood pressure remained similar to, or lower than, those measured while participants were taking the drugs. The main marker of excess aldosterone production remained 99% below its pretreatment level, and blood pressure was, on average, 25 points lower. Researchers reported partial or complete resolution of hypertension, with almost a quarter of participants having normal blood pressure without taking any other medication.
Mason Freeman, Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School, initiated the original study while medical director at Cincor. He said, “This follow-up study led by Dr. Brown has generated some extraordinary and unexpected findings. The sustained remission in the biochemical markers of the hyperaldosterone state, combined with much improved blood pressure levels, offers the very exciting possibility that many patients with primary aldosteronism may be able to be treated with a once-a-day pill, perhaps for a limited period of time, and obtain similar benefits to what we now achieve only after invasive diagnostic testing and major adrenal surgery.”
Could longer treatment eliminate hormone-producing cells?
Aldosterone synthase inhibitors had previously been tested in larger studies of people with hypertension. Those studies generally involved shorter treatment periods of 6 to 12 weeks, with outcomes measured while people were still taking the medication. Following patients after a 6- to 12-month course revealed the possibility that the treatment’s effects could outlast the medication itself.
One possible explanation dates to a 2005 experiment in mice. When scientists deleted the gene responsible for producing aldosterone synthase, the cells that make aldosterone disappeared. Researchers at Queen Mary predicted that blocking the enzyme for a prolonged period might have a similar effect in humans, potentially removing the source of excess hormone production.
Morris Brown, the study’s lead author and Professor of Endocrine Hypertension at Queen Mary, said, “While duly cautious about our findings because of the pragmatic nature of the study, they were predicted by previous experiments, and longer follow-up may justify a claim that a finite course of medication leads to infinite cure.
“EASI-treatment is unlikely to be the elixir for most patients with hypertension. But the possibility of tablets achieving a surgical cure has long been a holy grail for this common type of hypertension.”
The researchers are now leading a larger prospective clinical trial called ELIXIR to investigate whether EASI treatment can provide a lasting cure for people with primary aldosteronism. The trial will also use molecular imaging of the adrenal glands to examine whether prolonged treatment causes aldosterone-producing cells to disappear in humans.
Reference: “Hyperaldosteronism Remission after Extended Aldosterone Synthase Inhibition” by Morris J. Brown, Adina F. Turcu, Ramin Sam, Lawrence S. Kirschner, Oksana Hamidi, Aysegul Eren, Anat Ben-Shlomo, Wenyu Huang, Irina Bancos, Amir H. Hamrahian and Mason W. Freeman, 6 November 2026,
New England Journal of Medicine
DOI: 10.1056/NEJMc2611265

title: Scientists Crack a Decades-Old Mystery That Could Unlock Faster Internet
content:
Intrinsic optical properties of barium titanate revealed by Mueller matrix ellipsometry. Credit: KAIST
When light carries data through a communication device, absorption by the materials inside can weaken the signal. Engineers trying to build faster, more efficient devices need to predict how light will travel through those materials and how much will be lost before they commit to a design.
For a promising material called barium titanate, or BTO, those measurements have varied widely for decades. A KAIST-led research team has now clarified how it interacts with light, providing data that could help engineers design devices more reliably and reduce costly rounds of fabrication and redesign.
One crystal, different responses to light
BTO offers a useful way to control light because applying an electric field changes its refractive index, a measure of how much light slows as it passes through a material. Its strong response to an electric field, known as the Pockels effect, makes it promising for optical modulators. These devices use electrical signals to control light and encode information onto it.
Structural characteristics of single-crystal barium titanate and a schematic of the optical constant measurements. (Top) Temperature-dependent changes in the crystal structure of BTO (left), domain alignment according to the polarization direction (center), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) results for the high-quality a-cut and c-cut single crystals used in the experiments (right). (Bottom) Analytical framework for precisely extracting the intrinsic optical properties of BTO over an ultra-broad spectral range from the ultraviolet to the far-infrared, combining reflection- and transmission-mode Mueller matrix spectroscopic ellipsometry with transmission spectra. Credit: KAIST
The difficulty is that a BTO crystal can contain small regions, called domains, with different crystal orientations. Those regions can interact with light differently, so measuring them together blends their responses. That makes it harder to determine the material’s underlying optical properties and predict how it will behave in a device.
To reduce that mixing, the team led by Professor Min Seok Jang of KAIST’s School of Electrical Engineering examined two types of single-crystal BTO samples with relatively uniform domain orientations. The researchers used Mueller-matrix spectroscopic ellipsometry, a technique that measures changes in light’s polarization, or the orientation of its electric-field vibrations, when it reflects from or passes through a material. Those changes provide information about how the material affects light.
Intrinsic complex refractive index of tetragonal BTO determined over a broad spectral range. (Top) Refractive index and extinction coefficient of single-crystal BTO for ordinary and extraordinary rays, derived from the ultraviolet to the far-infrared. (Middle and bottom left) Optical absorption in the ultraviolet region, where electronic transitions occur (Tauc plot), and the refractive index and birefringence from the visible to the near-infrared, including telecommunication wavelengths. (Middle and bottom right) Polarization-resolved transmittance spectra of a single-crystal sample measured in the infrared transparency window, and the weak absorption coefficients derived from them. Credit: KAIST
Their analysis covered wavelengths from 190 nanometers (nm) to 40 micrometers (μm), spanning the ultraviolet to the far-infrared. Because BTO interacts with light differently across that range, the researchers divided it into three spectral regions and used an analytical approach suited to each. They determined how the refractive index and absorption properties vary with both wavelength and crystal orientation.
The team also developed a method for calculating the overall optical response of a crystal containing differently oriented domains. Using the orientations and relative proportions of those domains, the method accounts for the mixed internal structure that had made BTO’s properties difficult to establish.
(From left) Ph.D. candidate Jiwon Kang from KAIST, Dr. Nina Hong from J.A. Woollam Co., Professor Harry A. Atwater from Caltech, and Professor Min Seok Jang from KAIST. Credit: KAIST
Measuring light loss in nearly transparent barium titanate
Even in the wavelength range where BTO is nearly transparent, the researchers were able to quantify very weak absorption. They combined ellipsometry with separate transmittance measurements, which record how much light passes through a sample, to determine extinction coefficients as low as approximately 10⁻⁵ in the 2–10 μm range. The extinction coefficient describes how strongly a material absorbs light, with smaller values indicating weaker absorption.
Together, these measurements help answer two practical questions about a waveguide, a structure that guides light through a device. The refractive index helps designers predict how the light will travel, while the extinction coefficient helps them estimate how much will be lost to absorption. Engineers can use the data to assess devices of different sizes and shapes before fabrication. Potential applications include communications modulators, devices that generate light at new wavelengths, and circuits that process quantum information using light.
KAIST, led by President Choongsik Bae, announced the work on November 8. The study was conducted in collaboration with Professor Harry A. Atwater’s team at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), the Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS), and U.S.-based J.A. Woollam Co.
“This study reveals the optical response of barium titanate, which had long remained unclear, and provides a reliable reference for how the material interacts with light,” said Professor Min Seok Jang. He added that the findings are expected to contribute to optical communication devices that reduce light loss and enable faster data transmission, as well as quantum photonic devices that require precise control of light.
Reference: “Broadband Optical Characterization of Tetragonal Barium Titanate by Mueller-Matrix Spectroscopic Ellipsometry” by Jiwon Kang, Nina Hong, Christopher M. Yi, Yun Su Go, Martin Thomaschewski, Hwi Je Woo, Prachi Thureja, Junghoon Jahng, Harry A. Atwater and Min Seok Jang, 20 October 2026,
ACS Photonics
DOI: 10.1021/acsphotonics.6c01514

title: Scientists Discover Mysterious New Fish in the Red Sea – and Have Never Seen It Again
content:
Freshly collected Trimma charon sp. nov., paratype, live, ROMI118237, 12.1 mm SL. Credit: Viktor N. Peinemann
Scientists discovered a tiny new fish species in the Red Sea but have never found it again, suggesting it may live mostly on deeper reefs that remain largely unexplored.
In Greek mythology, Charon ferried the dead across a river into the underworld. People were traditionally buried with a coin to pay for the crossing. That tradition helped inspire the name of a newly described fish species from the northern Red Sea, Charon’s pygmygoby (
Trimma charon
“One of the most striking features of the new species is the golden spots scattered across its tail fin,” said study leader Viktor Nunes Peinemann of King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) in Saudi Arabia. “They cover most of the fin and resemble small gold coins.”
The tiny fish is translucent, with a broad orange-red stripe and an unusual four-part eye. The two known specimens measure just 12 and 17 millimeters long, roughly half an inch and two-thirds of an inch.
Photo collage of each Red Sea species of Trimma. Credit: V.N. Peinemann
A possible relative across two oceans
The new species resembles the pallid pygmygoby (
Trimma anaima
), a fish found from East Africa to the Pacific but never recorded in the Red Sea. Genetic data suggest the two are close relatives, although further work is needed to confirm that relationship.
“While one species seems to have spread across much of the Indian and Pacific Oceans, its closest relative appears to have stayed in the Red Sea and evolved separately for millions of years,” said Peinemann.
Two specimens hint at a deeper habitat
Researchers collected the two specimens in May 2023 at Walih Island, at the entrance to a cave on a steep reef slope. They were found 30 meters, about 98 feet, below the surface, the maximum depth of the team’s scientific diving. Extensive searches of similar habitats since then have produced no further sightings. “So far, the entire species is known from only a single encounter and two specimens,” said Peinemann.
Trimma avidori – an abundant Red Sea species. Credit: V.N. Peinemann
The team suspects that the encounter took place at the shallow edge of the species’ range. The fish may be more common on largely unexplored mesophotic reefs below 30 meters, where sunlight is faint. That possible habitat provides another connection to its mythological namesake.
“These dark, deeper, unexplored reefs could be viewed as a kind of ‘underworld’ beneath the shallow, well-lit, and better studied reefs most of us are more familiar with,” he said.
“Red Sea reefs below that depth almost certainly hold more undiscovered gobies.”
Many pygmygobies appear confined to the Red Sea
The discovery brings the number of known
species in the Red Sea to 11, making it the region’s most species-rich goby genus. At least nine appear to live nowhere else in the world. To help researchers distinguish them, the paper provides an illustrated identification key to all 11 species, along with photographs and field notes describing where each lives.
In situ photographs of Red Sea Trimma species. A. T. avidori; B. T. filamentosus; C, D. T. barralli; E. T. sheppardi; F. T. quadrimaculatum. All photographs were taken in the Red Sea. Credit: V.N. Peinemann (panels A, D); by F. Krasovec (panel B); by S.V. Bogorodsky (panels C, E, F)
The study is published in the open-access journal
. Peinemann is based in the Marine Science Program within KAUST’s Division of Biological and Environmental Science and Engineering. His co-authors are Matthew D. Tietbohl Talas and Michael L. Berumen of KAUST, and Sergey V. Bogorodsky of the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, Germany.
“Knowing which species are present, how to accurately identify them, and where they live, is the most foundational step to building a stronger understanding of these species and ecosystems,” said Peinemann. “They still have many secrets and deserve much more attention.”
Reference: “Trimma charon, a new species of pygmygoby (Teleostei, Gobiidae) from the Red Sea with a key to the Red Sea species of the genus” by Viktor N. Peinemann, Sergey V. Bogorodsky, Matthew D. Tietbohl Talas and Michael L. Berumen, 24 September 2026,

title: A 6-Million-Year-Old Whale Had a Face So Strange Scientists Thought It Was Crushed
content:
The head of Scaphokogia huachafo has a distinctive, asymmetrical forehead structure for sound production and directional echolocation while foraging on the seafloor. Credit: Jaime Bran Sarmiento
A newly identified prehistoric whale had unusual adaptations that may have allowed it to hunt along the seafloor millions of years ago.
An ancient whale that lived millions of years ago had a skull so dramatically distorted that its face appeared pushed to one side. Its bony nostrils were displaced entirely to the left, and its oversized snout curved sharply downward. Scientists have identified the animal as
Scaphokogia huachafo
, an extinct pygmy sperm whale with the most extreme facial asymmetry ever documented in a cetacean.
The fossil dates to the Late Miocene, approximately 6.3 to 5.6 million years ago, and belonged to a whale measuring about 2.7 meters (8.9 feet) long. Researchers believe its skull may also represent the greatest facial asymmetry known in any mammal.
Why This Ancient Whale Had Such an Unusual Skull
Most vertebrates have skulls that are approximately symmetrical, with corresponding structures on either side of the head. Toothed whales are an exception. Their skulls have evolved asymmetrical shapes to accommodate specialized organs involved in producing sound and echolocation, allowing them to navigate and detect prey underwater.
“Cranial asymmetry in toothed whales is directly linked to the development of fatty structures in the forehead that are involved in sound production. But in
Scaphokogia huachafo
, this asymmetry went far beyond the area around the blowhole. Both bony nostrils are shifted entirely to the left side of the skull, while the facial bones differ dramatically in size and position. The skull looks completely crooked,” explains Aldo Benites-Palomino, lead author of the study. He investigated the fossil during his doctoral research at the University of Zurich and is now an assistant professor at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU).
The entire structure of the skull and neck of Scaphokogia huachafo was designed to point its snout directly toward the seafloor. Credit: Jaime Bran Sarmiento
Built to Hunt Along the Seafloor
The whale’s unusual anatomy suggests a feeding strategy very different from that of modern sperm whales, which pursue squid in deep ocean waters.
Scaphokogia huachafo
appears to have been adapted for searching for food along the bottom of shallow coastal seas. Its thick, tubular snout contained dense bone and hardened cartilage that added weight toward the front of its body. The snout angled downward by 31 degrees, while reconstructions of the joint between the skull and first neck vertebra suggest the animal could lower its head by as much as 55 degrees.
“The entire cranio-cervical complex is modified to point the snout directly toward the bottom,” explains Gabriel Aguirre-Fernández, study co-author and doctoral advisor at the University of Zurich. “The combination of dense bone, the downward-curving snout and the flexible neck articulation allowed the animal to move directly above the seabed and feed close to the sediment.”
Unlike some modern marine mammals that forage along the bottom,
Scaphokogia
lacked specialized facial whiskers and visual adaptations associated with locating prey in sediment. Researchers therefore suspect it relied on its unusually developed biosonar system to detect food hidden in soft seabed deposits. This remains a hypothesis based on its anatomy rather than direct evidence of its hunting behavior. Its specialized ecological niche apparently disappeared as ocean conditions changed near the end of the Miocene.
A Fossil Skull That Looked Almost Too Strange to Be Real
The skull was recovered in the mid-1990s from the Pisco Formation in southern Peru, a desert region famous for exceptionally preserved marine fossils. Benites-Palomino encountered the specimen in 2015 while working on his bachelor’s thesis at the Museo de Historia Natural in Lima. Its extreme shape initially raised the possibility that geological forces had distorted the skull after the animal died.
“The initial suspicion with skulls this distorted is always taphonomy – that the specimen may have been flattened or twisted by sediment pressure over millions of years,” says Benites-Palomino. “But the sutures are fully closed, and there are no fractures, pathologies or deformations elsewhere on the skull. This was genuine biology, not a result of poor preservation.”
A Peruvian Name for an Extraordinary Whale
The researchers chose a species name that reflects the animal’s unconventional appearance.
Huachafo
comes from Peruvian Spanish and describes something extravagant, flashy, bizarre, or aesthetically excessive.
“In Peru,
huachafo
is an everyday word for anything that is flashy, over-the-top, bizarre, extravagant, or difficult to categorize aesthetically,” says Benites-Palomino.
“When we looked at the proportions of this whale – with its face strongly shifted to the left and its oversized, downward-curving snout – it broke every rule of symmetry and elegance seen in living cetaceans. Its anatomy is so extravagant and odd that
huachafo
seemed the perfect name for it.”
Reference: “Extreme cranial asymmetry in extinct benthic feeding sperm whales” by Aldo Benites-Palomino, Marcelo R. Sánchez-Villagra, Florencia Paolucci, Jorge Vélez-Juarbe, Alberto Collareta, Apolline Alfsen, Alton Dooley, Dan Omura, Mario Urbina, Rodolfo Salas-Gismondi and Gabriel Aguirre-Fernández, 9 November 2026,
Communications Biology

title: CT Scans Reveal the Secret of a Mysterious 400-Year-Old Lock
content:
The brass lock, discovered as part of the Ann Francis treasure hoard, has remained firmly locked since the ship was wrecked off the Welsh coast in 1583. Credit: Amgueddfa Cymru
X-ray scans cracked an Elizabethan padlock’s code, revealing how a centuries-old security mechanism worked without damaging an unusually well-preserved piece of maritime history.
For more than 400 years, a brass combination lock recovered from a shipwreck off the Welsh coast kept its secret. Lost when a violent storm wrecked the
Ann Francis
, the remarkably well-preserved Elizabethan lock still had working letter dials, but no one knew the four-letter combination needed to open it.
Opening it more than 400 years later meant working out its four-letter code without damaging an exceptionally well-preserved Elizabethan artifact, a challenge that brought museum specialists together with researchers more accustomed to studying bones.
The dials still turned after centuries
The lock came from the
Ann Francis
, which was returning from Spain when a ferocious storm blew it off course on the evening of December 28, 1583. The ship wrecked on Margam Beach, near Port Talbot, leaving its extraordinary cargo buried beneath the sand for centuries.
Dredging and storms eventually stripped away layers of sand, exposing traces of the sixteenth-century hoard. Metal detectorist Peter Hughes discovered most of it over 21 years, between 1996 and 2017. The finds, recovered by Hughes and other metal detectorists, were subsequently acquired by Amgueddfa Cymru (Museum Wales).
“When I found the lock, I was immediately astonished by the incredible workmanship and its astonishing condition. When I moved the ring dials of the combination, they turned with ease after over 400 years beneath the sands, and I was left in disbelief. I also remember being left excited at the prospect of finding wonderful things from the treasure chest it once locked,” said Hughes, finder of the hoard.
What the lock once protected remains uncertain. Researchers believe it secured a small chest containing valuable items, and its position near a collection of Spanish silver coins and two coin weights recovered from the wreck offers some clues. It may have guarded those objects or a chest holding valuables that did not survive, such as documents or textiles.
X-rays reveal the lock’s hidden code
To investigate the mechanism, museum experts worked with specialists at Cardiff University using micro-CT, a form of X-ray imaging that can reveal fine details inside an object. Dr. David Williams, a postdoctoral research associate based at the Musculoskeletal Biomechanics Research Facility in the university’s School of Engineering, explained the advantage of examining the lock this way.
“Micro-CT scanning allowed us to look inside the lock without damaging it.”
The task was to connect the letters visible on the outside with the concealed parts that determined whether the lock would open. Williams could examine those relationships in the scan, then pass the combination to the museum team for the physical test.
“By creating a detailed 3D image of the internal mechanism, I could see how the notches lined up with the letters and identify the exact combination. We normally use this technology to study bones and other biological structures, so investigating a 400-year-old padlock was certainly a first for us. I had to wait until later that evening for the museum team to test the combination, so getting the message that we’d cracked it was incredibly satisfying,” said Williams.
The four letters were ANCE, and when the museum team tested the combination, the centuries-old lock opened.
“It’s not every day you get to solve a 400-year-old mystery!” Williams said.
The code’s meaning remains a mystery
Its remarkable condition and connection to a shipwreck with a known date make the lock especially valuable as a historical find. Deciphering the combination also leaves a more personal question about whoever chose those letters.
“Elizabethan combination locks are known in Britain, but this one is in exceptionally good condition and is associated with a dated wreck, making it a unique find and the code a tantalizing mystery to solve. Of course, now we’ve solved it, we are left wondering if the code meant something to its owner,” said Alastair Willis, senior curator for numismatics and the Welsh economy at Amgueddfa Cymru.
The lock is currently on display at the National Waterfront Museum in Swansea alongside other artifacts from the Ann Francis hoard. They include rare gold coins dating from the reign of Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain and a boatswain’s whistle recovered from the wreck.

title: Stonehenge’s Mysterious Six-Ton Stone Has Scientists Searching Across Britain
content:
A new geological study has ruled out several possible origins of Stonehenge’s Altar Stone, leaving scientists with fresh clues to one of the monument’s oldest mysteries. Credit: Stock
Stonehenge’s six-ton Altar Stone has led scientists from Wales to Scotland, yet even its most detailed geological examination has failed to reveal where it came from.
Scientists have spent more than a century trying to determine where Stonehenge’s six-ton Altar Stone came from. Once thought to originate in Wales, the massive sandstone slab has since been traced geologically to northeast Scotland, but its exact source remains unknown. Now, the most comprehensive geological investigation yet has ruled out several proposed locations and provided new clues to guide the search.
Searching For A Geological Match
The latest investigation brought together observations of the Altar Stone itself and detailed examinations of fragments held in museum collections. By comparing its structure, mineral content, chemical composition, and isotopic characteristics, the team assembled a set of identifying features that potential sources must match.
Professors Richard Bevins and Nick Pearce with the Altar Stone. Credit: Aberystwyth University
No location examined so far in northeast Scotland’s Orcadian Basin has met all those criteria. That leaves the stone’s birthplace unresolved but gives future fieldwork a clearer target. Study leader Duncan Pirrie, emeritus professor at the University of South Wales, said:
“This is the most comprehensive geological investigation of the Altar Stone ever undertaken. By combining a wide range of analytical techniques, we have built the clearest picture yet of the stone’s composition and tested the leading theories about its origins. So far, none of the locations examined have the same set of characteristics as the Altar Stone. That tells us the search is not over, but we are now far better equipped to focus on the areas most likely to yield an answer.”
The findings build on earlier work that redirected the search away from Wales. Richard Bevins, honorary professor in Aberystwyth University’s Department of Geography and Earth Sciences, said:
“For almost a century, the prevailing view was that the Altar Stone came from west Wales. Our previous research overturned that assumption and pointed instead to Scotland as the most likely source. This latest study significantly refines the search by identifying the specific geological characteristics we need to look for, allowing future investigations to be targeted more effectively. With each new piece of evidence, we move closer to solving one of Stonehenge’s most enduring mysteries.”
The Altar Stone lies flat on the ground, sunk into the grass beneath the collapsed upright of the Great Trilithon and its lintel. Credit: Professor Nick Pearce, Aberystwyth University.
Nick Pearce, emeritus professor of geochemistry in the same department at Aberystwyth University, emphasized the value of eliminating candidates: “In a geological detective story such as this, ruling out potential source areas is just as important as identifying new ones. Every location eliminated narrows the search and brings us closer to discovering where the Altar Stone originated. The stone is unique among those at Stonehenge, and tracing its source would provide valuable new insights into its remarkable journey to Salisbury Plain thousands of years ago.”
Tracing A Prehistoric Engineering Feat
Stonehenge took shape through several construction phases between around 3000 and 1600 BC. Moving its stones across great distances was part of that achievement: the smaller bluestones traveled approximately 225 kilometers (140 miles) from west Wales.
Establishing where the Altar Stone began would give researchers a crucial geographical anchor for investigating how it reached the monument. The researchers hope that fingerprint will ultimately lead them to the source and shed new light on the effort behind one of prehistory’s most remarkable engineering achievements.
Reference: “Searching for the origin of the Stonehenge Altar Stone: new sedimentological, petrographical, mineralogical, geochemical and isotopic constraints” by Duncan Pirrie, Richard E. Bevins, Rob A. Ixer, Nick J. G. Pearce, Peter Turner, Matthew R. Power, Stephen Hillier, Andrew C. Morton, Ian Saunders, Sergio Andò, Marta Barbarano, Andrew Horbury and Gregory D. Price, 5 November 2026,
Journal of the Geological Society
DOI: 10.1144/jgs2026-090

title: Ancient Tomb Reveals That People Were Getting High on Cannabis 2,800 Years Ago
content:
Scientists have uncovered 2,800-year-old evidence of people getting high on cannabis, hidden in an ancient Siberian tomb filled with clues to mysterious burial rituals. Credit: Shutterstock
The oldest directly dated evidence of intoxicating cannabis use comes from a Scythian tomb, suggesting the plant’s mind-altering effects had a place in ancient burial rituals.
About 1,000 cannabis seeds recovered from a princely tomb in southern Siberia could not, on their own, tell archaeologists whether anyone had used the plant to get high. Cannabis, one of today’s most commonly used psychoactive plants, has also supplied oil, fiber, and medicine, and its flowers, leaves, and resins rarely survive to help distinguish among prehistoric uses.
The tomb, in the South Siberian Republic of Tyva, belonged to high-ranking members of Scythian society, a horse-riding culture of the Eurasian steppe. Researchers investigating the burial found another source of evidence in preserved human hair from its central chamber.
The Tunnug 1 archaeological excavation site in southern Siberia. Credit: T. Wallace
Dr. Gino Caspari, an archaeologist at the University of Bern’s Institute of Archaeological Sciences and the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology in Jena, Germany, led the international research team and is the lead author of the study, published in
. “The molecular traces in the hair and the cannabis seeds come from the same grave and suggest that cannabis was used for its intoxicating properties,” he says.
The cannabis seeds are not easy to spot in the excavation context. Credit: T. Wallace
Cannabis and sacrifice in a Scythian tomb
In an earlier publication, the team described the remains of 18 horses that had once been arranged on the burial mound. Several dozen additional horse sacrifices and scattered human bones have since come to light. “In this princely tomb, the burials were accompanied by extensive horse sacrifices and, most likely, human sacrifices as well,” says Caspari.
When photographed under good lighting, the seeds reveal a characteristic net-like pattern that allows for their identification as cannabis. Credit: Caspari et al.
Hair preserves evidence of cannabis use
To investigate whether cannabis compounds had entered the bodies of people buried there, the researchers analyzed the hair using high-resolution mass spectrometry and other methods. Mass spectrometry helps distinguish compounds by the mass and electrical charge of their molecules or fragments. Several hair samples produced clear signals consistent with cannabinol, or CBN, a compound that can form through the oxidation of tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC, the main intoxicating compound in cannabis. The team also detected weak signals whose masses were consistent with THC.
Preserved human hair from the graves made it possible to detect cannabis use. Credit: Caspari et al.
“This study is particularly insightful because it combines the analysis of plant remains with molecular traces in the human body,” says Caspari.
The researchers interpret the hair results as evidence of cannabis use, although the analyses cannot reliably establish how much was consumed or determine with certainty how its active compounds entered the body, such as through inhalation or ingestion. Later archaeological sites in Central Asia have yielded chemical residues of cannabinoids, compounds found in cannabis, in vessels and on heated stones that clearly indicate inhalation. The Tyva hair samples do not establish a particular method of consumption.
A site plan of the central burial area of the Tunnug 1 princely tomb. Credit: Caspari et al.
Ancient cannabis potency remains unknown
The recovered seeds likely came from wild plants, and the findings do not reveal how much THC those plants contained. It also remains unclear whether people specifically cultivated cannabis for its psychoactive properties or selected or cultivated plants for higher levels of active compounds.
The team is continuing its investigation. “We have already begun sequencing some of the plant samples,” says Caspari. “DNA preservation is excellent in this case. This will help us learn more about the history of the domestication and spread of this crop soon.”
Researcher at the Institute of Archaeological Sciences (IAW) of the University of Bern and the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology in Jena, Germany. Credit: Luis Moreira
Reference: “Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago” by Gino Caspari, Timur Sadykov, Daria Fomicheva, Jegor Blochin, Dominic Armbruster, Oliver Happel, Natalia Ryabogina, Kseniia Boxleitner and Robert Spengler, 5 November 2026,

title: GCL-ET and CATL say Fujian truck charging station is first to use perovskite tandem PV
content:
GCL-ET and CATL say Fujian truck charging station is first to use perovskite tandem PV
GCL Energy Technology
(GCL-ET), the energy technology arm of GCL Group, and QIJI Energy, CATL’s heavy-duty truck battery-swapping subsidiary, have commissioned a demonstration station in Ningde, Fujian province. According to the companies, it is China’s first use of perovskite tandem PV in a heavy-duty truck charging and battery-swapping setting. The announcement does not say how much of the station’s generating capacity is perovskite tandem.
The site pairs a 94 kW wind-solar system with 930 kWh of storage and supports battery swapping in about five minutes and MW-scale fast charging. The companies expect it to use 120 MWh of renewable electricity a year and avoid roughly 72 tonnes of carbon emissions. The station connects to GCL-ET’s virtual power plant platform, which uses AI to coordinate generation, storage, and charging loads for grid response and market participation.
CATL is also said to be among the strategic investors in
GCL’s perovskite business
, which has attracted investment across several rounds, most recently a
D1 financing round
. The company has also launched a
gigawatt-scale tandem module manufacturing facility
in Kunshan.

title: Yanhe puts three more perovskite solar modules into orbit for space testing
content:
Yanhe puts three more perovskite solar modules into orbit for space testing
Yanhe Technology
has placed three of its own space photovoltaic modules into a 535 km sun-synchronous orbit, launched on November 7 aboard a Ceres-2 Y3 rocket. Two tandem modules, one perovskite-crystalline silicon and one perovskite/CIGS, are carried on the North University of China-1 satellite, while a flexible perovskite module is aboard the Yunyao-1 28 satellite.
Image credit: Yanhe Technology
The tandem modules will undergo power conversion efficiency and stability testing in a real space environment under dawn-dusk orbital conditions, where the satellite tracks the day-night terminator and receives near-continuous illumination. The flexible module will capture images during in-orbit thermal cycling while the company monitors how particle radiation and other factors affect its power output and reliability.
This is Yanhe’s second space validation campaign in two months, following
a flexible perovskite module launched aboard the Tianyi-52 satellite on September 17
for long-term performance monitoring and testing of its adaptability to the space environment. In October the company established a joint laboratory with the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology covering perovskite solar cells, space PV, orbital energy systems, flexible solar devices and new PV materials, adding to
an earlier joint perovskite-silicon tandem lab with Soochow University

title: 详细解读龙源电力3GW组件框架采购开标价格-索比光伏网
content:
近日，索比光伏网获悉，龙源电力2026年第一批光伏组件设备框架采购公开招标已开标。
此前，10月14日，龙源电力曾在国能e招平台发布6GW的组件框架采购招标计划，但两周后（10月28日），他们发布变更公告，将采购容量压缩到原先的一半，只保留3GW。
可以看到，除海上光伏组件招标容量未受影响外，陆上光伏的招标容量从5GW压缩到2GW，只保留40%。其中，高效标段从3.5GW压缩到1.5GW，保留比例42.86%；中效标段从1.5GW压缩到0.5GW，保留比例33.33%。这在一定程度上体现了招标方在2027年项目投资类型、产品选型方面的倾向。
本次招标中，各标段的参与情况、报价区间、均价见下表：
从具体投标价格表来看，可以得到以下信息：
1.Top10企业不再坚守高价策略，甚至部分Top5-10企业在报价时明显更积极、抢单意愿强烈。事实上，7个标段中4个标段的最低价都由同一家Top10品牌报出，且每个标段都有至少4家Top4/Top10企业的报价在整体均价以下。考虑到2026-2027年下游需求恢复速度较慢，但几乎所有企业都有保市场份额的诉求，相关企业报价偏低在我们的意料之中。
2.有14家企业同时参与海上光伏标段和陆上光伏高效标段，价差-0.8~3.7分/W，平均为0.84分/W。具体看，2家企业对海上光伏组件和陆上光伏组件给出相同报价，4家企业的海上光伏组件价格更低，体现出他们对海上光伏项目的强烈诉求。其余绝大多数企业海上光伏组件只比陆上光伏组件贵不超过2分/W，场景溢价相对较低。
3.有16家企业同时参与陆上高效标段和中效标段，2家企业只参与高效标段，5家企业只参与中效标段，体现了不同企业对产品效率分布情况的预期。
4.对于上面提到的16家同时参与陆上高效标段和中效标段的企业，同一企业不同标段的价差最低为0.02分/W，最高为8.74分/W，分布较为分散，不低于半数企业价差在3~6分/W之间。需要强调，不能把“价差高”简单理解为“高效产品供应能力差”，还与企业技术迭代速度、折旧进程、产品定价机制和对利润的要求有关。本次招标中，标段间价差超过5分的企业有6家，对中效标段的报价全部低于均值，可以概括为“高效保利润、中效抢份额”策略。
5.各标段中的高价对整体分析有一定误导性。特别是标段6、标段7，如果将价格明显偏高（超过0.75元/W）的报价剔除，这两个标段的均价都在0.71元/W左右，更接近23.2%效率组件的实际市场行情。

title: Everything That Led to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s Fall
content: Jensen Huang is gone from Nvidia, the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago. The origins of that downfall go back to the 2010s—to when Alice Huang, one of the women with whom he allegedly had an affair, was setting herself up to become a major Nvidia customer. Their relationship went unnoticed for a long time, but then it became just one element in a growing array of scandals around Jensen that eventually led to his resignation on Wednesday. As the drama widened, it came to include two more alleged affairs, a confrontation at Jensen’s home and a fateful board meeting. Below, you’ll find a curated timeline of what happened. 2010s 2010s Kang Wei, Alice’s husband, meets Jensen. Kang was a private equity investor who bought video game companies, then Nvidia’s biggest market. 2015 2015 Megaspeed is incorporated in Singapore as 7Road International, the local arm of 7Road Holdings, a Shenzhen, China-based gaming company. March 2023 March 2023 7Road International is renamed Megaspeed. Alice becomes its managing director. She has no prior background in AI. June 2023 June 2023 Shanghai Century Litong is founded to rent out AI computing power, and one of its founding owners is a company in which Alice’s sister, Huang Yu, holds a stake. Months later, Century Litong says it has become an Nvidia preferred partner for cloud services, a status that comes with priority access to chips. October 2023 October 2023 Two weeks after the U.S. bans Nvidia’s A800 and H800 chips for China, Century Litong manages to acquire large volumes of the banned chips still sitting in distributors’ warehouses. Century Litong’s clients are China’s biggest tech companies. November 2023 November 2023 Megaspeed’s ownership moves from Huang Le Limited—a British Virgin Islands entity that refers to Alice’s Chinese name—to a Singapore company, Swiftdata. Alice steps down as managing director. Alice continues to act as Megaspeed’s leader, according to the Wall Street Journal . Early 2024 Early 2024 Alice meets Jensen at an annual Nvidia event in California, according to the Journal . Our reporting shows their relationship goes back to at least 2023. February 2024 February 2024 Megaspeed sets up a Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix. Some of the Nvidia hardware it buys later reaches Century Litong. June 2024 June 2024 The two Huangs are photographed together at a Taipei fbar with others during the Computex trade show. June 2024 June 2024 Speedmatrix begins receiving Nvidia hardware. Over the next year, it gets more than 200 shipments worth about $2 billion, much of it traced to a subsidiary of Inspur, a blacklisted Chinese server maker. September 2024 September 2024 U.S. Commerce officials inspect a Megaspeed-linked data center in Malaysia and find Nvidia gear still in its boxes. May 22, 2025 May 22, 2025 Alice and Jensen attend a group dinner in Taipei. Footage from Agence France-Presse and Taiwan’s Central News Agency shows Alice kissing Jensen on the cheek before they leave in the same car, though the images do not attract public scrutiny at this time. August 2025 August 2025 Nvidia’s general counsel contacts Commerce investigators about a probe into Megaspeed, which later moves to the Justice Department. Oct. 9, 2025 Oct. 9, 2025 The New York Times first reports on Megaspeed, Alice and her ties to Jensen. The U.S. and Singapore confirm they are investigating Megaspeed. The connections between Jensen and Megaspeed do not attract major public attention. Late 2025 Late 2025 President Donald Trump is briefed on U.S. intelligence agencies’ findings that Alice was a Chinese intelligence asset who was delivering updates to Beijing on her relationship with Jensen. Trump takes no action. Spring 2026 Spring 2026 A classified memo overseen by Secretary of State Marco Rubio warns that Alice was recruited by Chinese intelligence to target Jensen. Oct. 29, 2026 Oct. 29, 2026 The Times reports U.S. officials earlier in the year found Jensen had a “close relationship” with Alice and that he was the target of a Chinese spy plot—revelations that draw major attention to Jensen’s relationship with Megaspeed. He tells Bloomberg his dealings with Megaspeed were “completely normal.” Nov. 5, 2026 Nov. 5, 2026 Three Congressional committee chairs ask Jensen to attend a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18 about his ties to Alice. Nov. 6, 2026 Nov. 6, 2026 The Financial Times reports U.S. officials believe Jensen and Alice had a romantic relationship. Soon after, Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, confronts Jensen at his home. Jensen confesses. Nov. 8, 2026 Nov. 8, 2026 Jensen apologizes to Nvidia employees for being unfaithful to his wife, without naming Alice. Nvidia’s board launches an independent investigation . Around this time, Jensen tells senior Nvidia executives that his relationship with Alice was his only affair. Nov. 9, 2026 Nov. 9, 2026 Trump says he and Jensen have discussed Alice—and that he asked Jensen if he knew Alice was a spy. Jensen denied he knew, according to Trump, who calls Jensen “a very honorable man.” Trump says the FBI had been investigating something related to Jensen. Nov. 9, 2026 Nov. 9, 2026 Nvidia’s board hires Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, a prominent white shoe law firm, to run an investigation led by Joon Kim, a former acting U.S. attorney, who previously investigated the sexual harassment scandal around former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo. Nov. 10, 2026 Nov. 10, 2026 The Information reports that Alice and her family built a network of companies in China and Singapore. Her relationship with Jensen helped move at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia chips, about 240,000 of them banned, into China. Nov. 10, 2026 Nov. 10, 2026 Silicon Valley leaders try to rally support for Jensen, including venture capitalist Ron Conway. “Jensen’s statements have shown grace and dignity to his family and the industry,” he writes . “We should be patient and wait for investigations by the board of directors and any government authorities to conclude.” Nov. 11, 2026 Nov. 11, 2026 The New York Times reports Huang had a second affair with an Nvidia employee who reported directly to him. That pushes Nvidia’s board to meet. Later in the evening, Jensen resigns. Nov. 12, 2026 Nov. 12, 2026 Nvidia names Colette Kress , the longtime chief financial officer, as interim CEO and says it will search for a permanent replacement among internal and external candidates. Harvey Jones, a board fixture, becomes the company’s first ever chair. Nov. 12, 2026 Nov. 12, 2026 The Senate bank committee asks Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify. Lutnick is underfire for Commerce’s supervision of U.S. export bans on Nvidia chips. Nov. 12, 2026 Nov. 12, 2026 Reuters reports that Huang had a third affair—with another Nvidia employee. title: Jensen Didn’t Create the AI Boom. It Created Him.
content: If you follow investors and reporters on X, you would get the sense that the resignation of Jensen Huang amounts to the end of the AI boom. A summary of my X feed Wednesday morning would go something like “I hope the Nvidia board knew what they were doing before ending the world as we know it.” But if you believe that to be true, you haven’t been paying attention. Because as much as Jensen created the AI boom (and clearly Nvidia’s GPU—the brains that trains AI models—did), the AI boom created Jensen. And that’s key to understanding the world that comes after his reign. Let me explain. Around four years ago, just as ChatGPT was launching, Silicon Valley needed a poster child. Social media wasn’t going that well for tech’s reputation, which was getting worse as its power grew.  Many founders and CEOs had either stepped aside or were eschewing the spotlight. But a new platform loomed. An incredibly powerful one called AI, but also one that very few knew what to do with. It was hard to explain to the public and, potentially, quite scary. But the center of this ecosystem had a somewhat nerdy-seeming CEO who people seemed to like. He talked in technical terms about scaling intelligence and painted a vision of an abundant future. And he liked to talk—to investors, reporters, government officials, you name it. Jensen became a leather-jacket clad rockstar to pump AI businesses to customers, investors and media on the podcast circuit. He was the relationship investors bragged to their LPs about. And he made those investors a lot of money! For reporters, he was the big get at a conference—a sign that you had clout. And he also held the keys to the most powerful technology of the era, so no one dared say a bad word about him publicly. He built the tech and the rest of the industry—companies, investors and media—built the myth that he wallowed in. And boy did he wallow. At a press conference last year, I grimaced when I saw him ask a reporter why the person didn’t bring him an award. I’ve covered the big egos of tech for more than twenty years. That was a first for me—even if he did mean it as a joke. So if you want to know what happens next, don’t be fooled by the idea that he is too big to fail. “Jensen” the myth wasn’t the reality. It was a myth that Jensen, along with his customers, investors and the media conspired to build. As we now know through some incredibly intrepid reporting, it was a myth that cloaked myriad affairs and, possibly, other impropriety. One of the world’s most powerful law firms is investigating him and more is likely to come out. So what happens to an industry without its rockstar? Something quite simple and quite good: competition. It was already coming. And despite the solid leadership under Jensen at Nvidia that will undoubtedly keep building great products, his departure leaves more openings for Google, AMD, Amazon and others that are already chomping at the bit. But the end of AI? A colossal mistake that will force the U.S to cede its technical dominance to China? Let’s cut the hyperbole. AI companies have big challenges. Americans overwhelmingly fear the technology and just voted to curb its growth. The technology is progressing at a speed that its own makers admit they cannot control. There are gaping governance holes across the industry as myriad young companies have become giants in a matter of months and years. And by this time next week, one of them, Anthropic, will be one of the most valuable public companies in the world. So, in the wake of Jensen’s downfall, I hope Silicon Valley can agree that the time for legends is over. It’s time for leadership.

title: 科学网-“中国药科大学星”小行星命名仪式举行
content:
“中国药科大学星”小行星命名仪式举行
11月14日下午，“中国药科大学星”小行星命名仪式在江宁校区会议中心二楼报告厅举行。中国科学院紫金山天文台副台长吴雪峰，行星科学和深空探测研究部主任、小行星命名委员会秘书长赵海斌，校党委书记戴建君，校长郝海平，相关职能部门及二级党组织负责人，校友代表及师生代表等共同见证命名仪式。仪式由校党委副书记、纪委书记陈文恩主持。
戴建君在致辞中向紫金山天文台以及所有为小行星发现、观测、提名工作的专家学者致以诚挚感谢与崇高敬意。他指出，小行星命名是一项具有国际性、历史性的崇高荣誉。建校九十年来，学校坚守“精业济群”校训，牢记兴药为民初心，为国家输送大批高素质药学人才，被誉为“中国生物医药人才摇篮”。“中国药科大学星”是镌刻在星空之上的勋章，更是激励全体师生探索未知、追求卓越的精神灯塔。他勉励全校师生以星为证、铭记初心，以星为帆、勇攀高峰，以星为炬、点亮青春，把这份星空赋予的荣誉转化为实干奋进的动力，聚焦生物医药领域难题攻坚克难，将个人理想融入民族复兴伟业，向着建设药学特色世界一流大学的目标奋勇前行。
吴雪峰宣读“中国药科大学星”国际命名公报，并代表紫金山天文台向学校致以热烈祝贺。他表示，中国药科大学历史悠久、特色鲜明，在药学界享有盛誉，为国家卫生健康事业作出了突出贡献。值此九十华诞之际，以小行星为学校命名，不仅是国际社会对学校的崇高礼赞，更是对学校90年辉煌历程的深切致敬。紫金山天文台愿与学校携手共进，在学科建设、人才培养和科研创新等方面深化合作，共同开创发展新格局。
随后，吴雪峰向学校颁发“中国药科大学星”命名证书。郝海平代表学校接收了证书，并在讲话中表示，有药的地方就有中国药大人的身影，一道道微光的身影逐渐汇聚成今天“中国药科大学星”璀璨的亮光。“中国药科大学星”在浩瀚宇宙持续运转，承载着九秩药大的办学荣光，寄托着兴药为民的理想。希望全体中国药大人仰望星空、脚踏实地，坚守立德树人使命，深耕生物医药领域，守护人民生命健康，让“精业济群”精神与“中国药科大学星”一同长久闪耀于宇宙苍穹。
仪式上，赵海斌详细介绍了“中国药科大学星”的发现过程与天体运行参数。该天体于2007年11月10日由盱眙观测站1.04米施密特型近地天体望远镜发现，后经多国天文台联合观测验证，历时近6年完成轨道精确测算，2013年获得国际小行星中心永久编号361707号。小行星轨道半长径2.674天文单位，绕太阳运行一周需要4.37年，运行速度每秒17.4公里，距离地球最远6.7亿公里、最近1.3亿公里。
最后，在与会人员的共同见证下，吴雪峰、赵海斌与戴建君、郝海平共同为“中国药科大学星”揭幕，宣布经国际天文学联合会批准，将国际编号361707号小行星正式命名为“中国药科大学星”。

title: 科学网-科技助农 中国科协帮扶山西农产品进京展销
content:
科技助农 中国科协帮扶山西农产品进京展销
11月12日至13日,“临岚好物进京·四季助农惠农”展销活动在中国科技会堂举办。岚县、临县特色农产品集中进京，通过线下展销、美食品鉴、大宗采购洽谈和线上多平台直播同步推进，借“双11”节点拓宽产销对接渠道。
活动由中国科协直属机关工会主办，中国农技协、中国科协驻临县岚县帮扶工作队承办，17家参展企业集中展示两地马铃薯制品、沙棘、红枣、玉米、小杂粮等特色农产品50余种，面向中国科协机关、直属单位工会会员及全国学会开放，销售额达18万余元。
展销活动现场。中国科协供图
活动开展多平台矩阵式线上展销和助农直播，中国农技协电商科技志愿服务队组织电商直播团队参与助农直播4场，同步开展“走基层帮销售”惠农行动，通过直播推介帮助两县科技小院、合作社、农户对接线上渠道，拓宽产品销路。10余家全国学会及科研院所、学会会员单位的后勤部门，与两县涉农企业现场洽谈，围绕产品标准、供应周期、质量追溯等环节达成合作共识。
与展销同步，活动邀请抖音官方讲师开展数字化营销专项培训，围绕短视频创作、直播引流转化、农货达人孵化授课，面向两县本土从业者、合作社带头人和返乡创业青年培训学员40余人，孵化本地主播和运营队伍，补齐数字化营销短板。
岚县、临县地处晋西黄土丘陵沟壑区，农特产品品质优良，但品牌影响力不足、产销渠道不畅。中国科协定点帮扶以来，持续在产业培育、技术引进、人才培养等方面投入力量。下一步将依托全国学会专家资源和数字助农平台，把消费端的市场反馈反向传导至生产端，推动帮扶地区特色产业标准化、品牌化发展，稳定带动农户增收，助力乡村全面振兴。
据悉，中国科协已连续帮扶吕梁地区41年，先后助力岚县于2019年、临县于2020年实现脱贫摘帽。2021年，中国科协农村专业技术服务中心扶贫工作处被党中央、国务院授予“全国脱贫攻坚先进集体”荣誉称号。

title: 科学网-研究发现动物市场病毒多样性更高、宿主关联更密
content:
研究发现动物市场病毒多样性更高、宿主关联更密
近日，广东省科学院动物研究所研究员陈金平团队与合作者，系统揭示了野外、养殖场及动物市场三类生态环境中的病毒多样性、群落结构与病毒-宿主关联特征。相关成果发表于《微生物组学》。
动物市场是野生动物、养殖动物与人类活动相互交汇的重要生态界面，不同动物宿主的聚集可能增加病毒共享与传播风险，但此前对三类环境下病毒群落差异及宿主间病毒关联模式仍缺乏系统认识。
不同生态环境中的病毒共享及宿主关联。研究团队供图
联合华大生命科学研究院副研究员王达希团队、广东省农业科学院动物卫生研究所研究员王晓虎团队，
采集广东省野外、养殖场及市场相关环境样品279份，利用宏转录组测序技术开展病毒组分析。动物来源样品涵盖15个宿主目，共鉴定出106个脊椎动物相关病毒谱系、259个病毒株，其中包括19个潜在新病毒。比较分析显示，三类生态环境的病毒群落组成存在显著差异，市场相关样品病毒丰度总体更高，表明动物市场是多种动物源病毒共同出现的重要生态场所。
病毒共享及网络分析进一步发现，野外、养殖场与市场相关动物之间存在不同程度的病毒共享，其中市场相关宿主的病毒—宿主关联更为广泛，在病毒共享网络中具有更高的连接度和中介中心性。研究还鉴定出38条具有已报道致病相关性的病毒序列，涉及13个病毒谱系，提示有必要加强重点动物源病毒的持续监测与针对性风险评估。
该研究揭示了动物市场在连接野生动物与养殖动物病毒生态网络中的重要作用，为理解不同生态环境下的病毒多样性与宿主关联模式提供了新证据，对构建“同一健康”（One Health）框架下的动物源病毒协同监测体系具有重要参考价值。
